name: beautiful-ios
description: Write, review, port, and enforce idiomatic native iOS apps in Swift 6 + SwiftUI written as code: three skills distilled from Apple's SwiftUI and concurrency documentation, the App Store guidance, and the facta iOS handbook, plus a drop-in SwiftLint and swift-format config.

interface.longDescription:
Three skills for native iOS developers on Swift 6 + SwiftUI written as code, distilled from Apple's SwiftUI and concurrency documentation, the App Store guidance, and the facta iOS handbook.

ios-best-practices guides new native code: views as code with no visual builders, Swift 6 strict concurrency and main-actor isolation, Swift packages that enforce the Domain/Data/UI/App layers, UDF with @Observable ViewModels, NavigationStack and validated deep links, GRDB and the outbox, Keychain secrets, APNs, MetricKit and the older-iPhone performance budget.

ios-review reviews a SwiftUI view, Observable ViewModel, package/target boundary, concurrency change, GRDB/outbox path, deep link, APNs handler, or diff and returns a prioritized report. Architecture and main-actor contracts rank above everything. Every finding cites a file and line, the rule it breaks, and the smallest fix.

ios-port ports a React Native, web, UIKit/storyboard or legacy screen to SwiftUI-as-code with the same behavior. It ports the original tests first and writes a PORTING.md.

The skills contain instructions and reference text only. They make no network calls and collect no data. When a Swift/Xcode toolchain is available, the skills run swift test, swiftlint, and xcodebuild on your project; without one, they work from the code alone. A drop-in SwiftLint and swift-format config is available in the GitHub repository.
capabilities: Review iOS code with cited rules
Port RN, web or UIKit screens to SwiftUI
defaultPrompt: Review this SwiftUI screen and list what to fix first
Port this React Native screen to SwiftUI
Fix the main-actor isolation in this ViewModel

publication.release_notes: Initial release: three iOS skills, the package and main-actor contract, and a proven SwiftLint config.
